Article Title: ‘I would have banned Sourav Ganguly’: Javagal Srinath on Steve Waugh’s wait during 2001 Eden Test toss
Article Text:
Sourav Ganguly and Javagal Srinath

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

CHENNAI: If Javagal Srinath had been the match referee when former India captain Sourav Ganguly famously kept his Australian counterpart Steve Waugh waiting at the toss during the 2001 Eden Gardens Test match, Ganguly may well have faced a suspension!“I would have banned Sourav for a few games,” Srinath said at an event here while recalling the incident, which has gone down in history as an act of gamesmanship that rattled Waugh and the Australian team during the course of the famous series that India won 2-1. Ganguly later said that he couldn’t find his blazer, leading to an impromptu delay.Srinath, however, praised Ganguly’s leadership, particularly his ability to nurture youngsters such as Yuvraj Singh, Harbhajan Singh and Virender Sehwag. He felt Indian cricket underwent a major transformation after the match-fixing scandal of the late 1990s, with players developing a collective resolve to restore the game’s image.“There was a bit of a resoluteness in each and every player to really put that image back and then prove to the world that cricket is superior, cricket is clean,” Srinath said. He recalled that between 1991 and 1997-98, India struggled to win abroad but things began changing from 1999 on.Looking back at the 2003 World Cup final against Australia, Srinath revealed that he had wanted India to bat first after a discussion within the team.“I was one of the guys who said we should always bat first and then put them under pressure,” he said. But Ganguly had a different view. And once the decision was made, Srinath said the team had to move on, but Australia were simply too strong.He recalled recommending Zaheer to selector Chandu Borde after watching the left-arm pacer take six wickets against Air India while representing the MRF Pace Foundation. When Borde jokingly asked what would happen to Srinath if Zaheer was picked, his response was simple: “If he’s good, he replaces me.”
Article Summary: Javagal Srinath says he would have banned Sourav Ganguly for keeping Steve Waugh waiting at the toss during the 2001 Eden Gardens Test match. He praised Ganguly's leadership, particularly his ability to nurture youngsters such as Yuvraj Singh, Harbhajan Singh and Virender Sehwag. He felt Indian cricket underwent a major transformation after the match-fixing scandal.

Article Title: Basant Meghwal’s historic silver, Shahnavaz’s bronze take India’s medal tally to three at World U20s
Article Text:
Basant Kumar Meghwal (Image: X/@afiindia)

Meghwal clears 2.21m for historic medal

Personal best caps impressive season

Shahnavaz wins bronze as India’s medal tally rises

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Arjunan finishes eighth

India’s medal tally reaches three

Indian high jumper Basant Kumar Meghwal created history by winning the silver medal in the men's high jump at the World Athletics U20 Championships in Eugene, Oregon, on Saturday. The 19-year-old from Anupgarh in Rajasthan's Sri Ganganagar district produced a lifetime-best effort of 2.21m to secure India's second medal of the championships and become the country's first high jumper to win a medal at the World Athletics U20 Championships.Meghwal was involved in a closely fought battle for the podium, with all three medalists managing to clear 2.21m but failing to go beyond 2.24m. With none of the athletes able to clear 2.24m in three attempts, the medals were decided through a countback based on their attempts at the previous height.Algeria's Younes Ayachi took the gold after clearing 2.21m on his first attempt. Meghwal secured silver by clearing the same height on his second attempt, while Great Britain's Otis Poole had to settle for bronze after taking three attempts to clear 2.21m.The silver medal caps an impressive season for Meghwal, who continues to make rapid progress on the international stage. His 2.21m clearance was a new lifetime personal best, adding another major achievement to his season after he won gold at the Asian U20 Athletics Championships earlier this year.India added another medal to their tally at the World Athletics U20 Championships as Shahnavaz clinched bronze in the men's long jump, taking the country's total haul at the championships to three. The 18-year-old produced his best effort of 7.84m in his third attempt to finish third in a closely contested final.Shahnavaz began the competition with a 7.67m effort before improving to 7.72m in his second attempt. He then delivered his best jump of the competition in his third attempt, clearing 7.84m to move into medal position. His remaining attempts were recorded at 7.52m, 7.83m and 5.37m, but his third-round effort was enough to secure the bronze medal.Italy's Daniele Inzoli won gold with a 7.97m jump, while Australia's Mason McGroder took silver with a personal-best 7.96m effort.India's other finalist, R.C. Jithin Arjunan, finished eighth with a best effort of 7.59m. Arjunan recorded the mark in both his first and fourth attempts but could not improve on it during the remainder of the competition.Shahnavaz's bronze added to an impressive medal haul for India in Eugene. Ashish Yadav opened India's account with a silver medal in the men's javelin throw on Friday. Basant Kumar Meghwal then created history by winning silver in the men's high jump with a personal-best 2.21m.
Article Summary: Basant Kumar Meghwal becomes India's first high jumper to win a medal at the World Athletics U20 Championships. The 19-year-old produced a lifetime-best effort of 2.21m to secure India's second medal of the championships. India's other finalist, R.C. Jithin Arjunan, finished eighth with a best effort of 7.59m.

Article Title: The Stateless Kings: How Chess preserves an ideal in a fractured world
Article Text:
Viktor Korchnoi (FIDE Photo)

Alireza Firouzja and Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa (Photo by Michal Walusza_Norway Chess)

Ian Nepomniachtchi and D Gukesh

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

FIDE’s official motto, Gens una sumus (we are one family), was adopted in 1952, almost three decades after the chess governing body was set up in 1924. On its face, the motto carries the naïve idealism of a mid-twentieth-century world recovering from the horrors of the Second World War.A hopeful attempt to frame a centuries-old game of simulated warfare as an instrument of global peace. Across more than seven decades of geopolitical upheavals, ideological iron curtains and border-redefining wars since 1952, chess has been forced to answer a recurring question: what happens to a family when its member nations tear each other apart?Global sport has followed a very predictable response to geopolitical conflicts. Athletes are routinely cancelled; lifelong pursuits of their craft are cut short by state actions they had no role in.FIDE, chess’s governing body, has let its motto guide its response to such moments. Guided by the simple reasoning that politics should not enter the game, FIDE has allowed dissidents, defectors, protesters and sanctioned players to play under a neutral flag that bears the federation’s logo. To trace this banner’s arc - from Viktor Korchnoi in 1978 to Alireza Firouzja and Ian Nepomniachtchi today - is to see how Gens una sumus has evolved from an idealistic slogan into a guiding principle.The lineage begins with Korchnoi, a man who tested the limits of political exile. In July 1976, after a tournament in Amsterdam, Korchnoi walked into a Dutch police station and requested political asylum, defecting from the Soviet Union. The Soviet state and the Soviet Chess Federation were apoplectic. Moscow demanded that FIDE strike Korchnoi’s name from the grandmaster lists and strip him of his right to challenge for the World Championship.Had FIDE acquiesced, it would have set a precedent, reducing the governing body to an extension of state power. Instead, under the leadership of its president, former World Champion Max Euwe, FIDE stood firm. Korchnoi was granted the right to compete under the FIDE flag.He qualified through the Candidates cycle as a stateless man, playing under the federation’s flag, and beat Tigran Petrosian, Lev Polugaevsky and Boris Spassky to earn his shot at challenging Anatoly Karpov for the World Championship.When Korchnoi sat across from Karpov in the famously tense 1978 World Championship match in the Philippines, he was living in Switzerland. He eventually lost 6-5 to Karpov. FIDE’s unyielding stance through the Korchnoi saga asserted its position that it would clear every hurdle to let chess players play.Four decades later, the FIDE flag found a new purpose. In December 2019, Firouzja, then a 16-year-old prodigy from Iran, found himself caught in a policy enforced by his home federation: a mandatory boycott requiring Iranian players to forfeit their games whenever they were paired against Israeli opponents.For a generational talent with ambitions of becoming world champion, state-mandated forfeits were a professional death sentence. Facing the prospect of not being able to play in the World Rapid and Blitz Championship in Moscow as Iran withdrew its players to enforce its policy, Firouzja made a courageous break. He registered for the tournament under the FIDE flag.Sitting quietly in Moscow with the neutral FIDE logo next to his name, the teenager marched to a silver medal behind Magnus Carlsen. FIDE’s umbrella enabled Firouzja’s brilliant trajectory to continue uninterrupted by state dogma, bridging his career until he eventually took French citizenship.FIDE faced its most complex test in the shadow of the war in Ukraine. Following the 2022 invasion, global sports authorities moved to isolate Russian and Belarusian athletes. While team events were banned, FIDE provided an expedited pathway for individual players to compete under the neutral FIDE banner.Take the case of Nepomniachtchi. In late 2021, bound by World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) sanctions against Russia, Nepomniachtchi contested his first World Championship match against Carlsen not under the Russian tricolour but under the neutral banner of the ‘Chess Federation of Russia’. Nepomniachtchi lost the 2021 championship to Carlsen.When Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Nepomniachtchi was one of 44 elite Russian grandmasters who signed an open letter to the Russian President opposing the war.At his next shot at the World Championship, in 2023 against China’s Ding Liren, Nepomniachtchi played under the blue FIDE flag.To the average person, a player under a neutral flag can look like a man without an identity. The opposite is true. When Nepomniachtchi sat in Astana, Firouzja in Moscow, or Korchnoi in Baguio, the neutral flag did not erase their identity. It protected the players from the geopolitics of their birthplaces.It would be naïve to assume that chess players are immune to political reality. Korchnoi lived through intense paranoia and state surveillance. Firouzja was forced to leave his homeland. Nepomniachtchi competed under the shadow of a devastating war he openly opposed.Gens una sumus is not a promise of an idyllic utopia; it is FIDE’s commitment to every chess player. It is a promise that when the real world fractures, there remains one arena where a person can step forward, shake their opponent’s hand and simply compete as an equal.Under the FIDE flag, stateless does not mean helpless. It means free to play.(Aarav Dengla is India’s 93rd Grandmaster. He is a keen observer and student of world history in general and chess history in particular.)
Article Summary: FIDE’s official motto, Gens una sumus (we are one family), was adopted in 1952, almost three decades after the chess governing body was set up. Since 1952, chess has been forced to answer a recurring question: what happens to a family when its member nations tear each other apart?

Article Title: ‘I can’t imagine the pain’: Rafael Nadal’s emotional tribute to Lionel Messi after father’s death
Article Text:
Rafael Nadal and Lionel Messi

Nadal and Messi: mutual admiration

De Paul delivers another emotional tribute

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Condolences have poured in from across the sporting world following the death of Lionel Messi ’s father, Jorge Messi, with tennis great Rafael Nadal among those to send an emotional message to the Argentine football icon and his family.Jorge Messi, who was 68, died on Friday in Rosario, Argentina, following a long-term illness. His death prompted an outpouring of tributes for the man who played a hugely influential role in the career of one of football’s greatest-ever players.Nadal, a lifelong football fan and admirer of Messi, took to X to offer his condolences, acknowledging the immense pain his fellow sporting legend must be experiencing.“Dear Leo, I can't imagine the pain you must be going through. I'm sending you all my love and my condolences to you and your entire family during this such difficult time. Rest in peace, Jorge,” Nadal wrote.The 22-time Grand Slam champion's message carried particular significance given Messi's own admiration for Nadal.Born and raised in Mallorca, Nadal grew up surrounded by football and was briefly torn between the sport and tennis before ultimately choosing the latter. His uncle, Miguel Angel Nadal, played for Barcelona and Spain, while the tennis legend has often spoken about his love for the game.Messi, meanwhile, has previously cited Nadal as an inspiration and drawn parallels between their approaches to their respective sports.“We are currently watching the Rafa Nadal series, and I really relate to him,” Messi told Spanish media in June.“I really like to play football, it is my passion since I was a child and when I am feeling good, I give my all. I think that we are very similar in that sense: I always want to give my all and feel good.”Nadal's message therefore came from one sporting icon to another at an extraordinarily difficult moment for Messi.Nadal was not the only major sporting figure to reach out to Messi.Inter Miami also sent its condolences to their captain and the Messi family, while Rodrigo De Paul paid tribute in a particularly poignant fashion during Miami's match against Monterrey.With Messi absent after returning to Argentina to be with his family, De Paul opened the scoring with a superb long-range strike. He then removed his Inter Miami shirt to reveal Messi's iconic No. 10 jersey underneath. The Argentina midfielder's gesture was a powerful reminder of the close friendship between the two players, who shared Argentina's 2022 World Cup triumph and were teammates again at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.For Messi, however, the sporting tributes came amid a deeply personal loss.Jorge was not only his father but also his agent and a central figure in his journey from a young footballer in Rosario to a global icon. He accompanied Messi to Barcelona for the trial that eventually led to his admission to La Masia and later helped manage his career and business affairs.
Article Summary: Lionel Messi's father, Jorge, died on Friday after a long-term illness. Tennis great Rafael Nadal has offered his condolences to Messi and his family. Inter Miami captain Rodrigo De Paul also paid tribute to Messi during his side's match against Monterrey.

Article Title: ‘We want to write our own World Cup history’: Craig Fulton on India’s bid to end 51-year wait for podium finish
Article Text:
India head coach Craig Fulton

How do you balance the weight of expectation of breaking a 51-year-old medal drought?

How was the conditioning camp in Switzerland?

You had a similar camp before the Paris Olympics...

How does the inclusion of youngsters like Yashdeep Siwach and Aditya Lalage enhance team balance?

Have dragflick specialists like Rajinder Singh and Sanjay eased the pressure on

Harmanpreet Singh

?

Defence has been the best form of attack for India...

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

How do you view the league games, especially the one against Pakistan?

BENGALURU: Being the coach of an Indian hockey team at the moment is hardly an enviable job. With the FIH World Cup followed immediately by the Asian Games, Craig Fulton’s side has a packed calendar to negotiate. Add to that the controversy over the change in the team’s jersey colour, which threatened to overshadow their World Cup campaign. The chief coach, however, insists the team is focused, with all its energies channelled towards achieving their first podium finish in 51 years. Excepts...We come into this World Cup not being the favourites. We are ranked seventh in the world and we’ve got a 5% chance of winning, which is fantastic. We start with all our eggs in the basket against Wales. We’re going to go full in for that game and take it one game at a time. There is no pressure on us. The only pressure is that we want to bring pride back to the World Cup from an Indian perspective, but also write our own piece of World Cup history from an Indian perspective.We had a team-building camp in Switzerland with mental conditioning specialist Paddy Upton . It was an amazing time together which has helped us set up how we want to operate in the next 3-4 weeks.Obviously we have a different challenge because we have two tournaments back-to-back. So it was about addressing how we manage the highs and lows of both and still come out on top.Two things happen when you move out of your own bubble. One, you realise the privilege of playing for your country and the immense pride that you can bring to your nation. You also have a very supportive govt, with SAI and Hockey India wanting the best for everyone in terms of performance. It’s about getting comfortable with the fact that you’ve been chosen for a reason. Also, it was about staying humble and realising that there is a process to be followed and we can’t jump to the final.It is about the balance of youth. It’s not only about results now. (We’re thinking) in terms of the LA Olympics (too). That was the big project with India ‘A’, to try and bring the next group of young, talented Indian players to the international level. Yashdeep and Aditya have been in the group for quite a while now. They’ve played almost two seasons with the Pro League and have taken their opportunity well. Also, they are fit, strong and bring a different dynamic.Harman got to a point where he took 80% of the penalty corners. He had 10 goals in Paris with penalty corners. That’s huge amount of responsibility. If we can place 2-3 other players around him, it doesn’t always depend on him. That’s what we’ve been trying to build for the last 18 months since Paris. We’re starting to get some traction there.It continues to do that. It evolves. We’re also very comfortable pressing. It’s another form of defence. We high-press and try to turn over the ball in the opposition half and then counter-attack from there.Our press-counter-perform philosophy has also evolved from the defendto-win approach. They’re very similar in the sense that you need a very good defence to survive at the international level. Even if you’re not scoring, as long as you’re not conceding, you stay in the game. But if you only have the all-out offensive and you’re not scoring and you can’t defend, then you lose games. This has been proven through the Paris Olympics.Apart from Wales, we also play England and Pakistan in the league phase. We played both teams in the Pro League. We’re quite happy with our pool just because we know the opposition. England are always a threat. We match up nicely against each other. Anytime we play Pakistan, it is exciting. That team is rebuilding. The match will improve the rivalry. There’s never a dull moment in a game against them.
Article Summary: Craig Fulton says India are not favourites for the FIH World Cup. India are aiming to break a 51-year-old medal drought at the tournament. Fulton's side play Wales, England and Pakistan in the league phase. India will also compete in the Asian Games in August.

Article Title: FIFA hits back at ‘concerted effort’ to undermine Gianni Infantino amid fresh allegations
Article Text:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino (AP Photo)

FIFA: ‘Repetition does not make an allegation true’

Infantino retains support outside Europe

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

FIFA has launched a strong defence of president Gianni Infantino, accusing unnamed critics of mounting a “concerted and ongoing effort” to undermine the governing body and its president amid fresh allegations concerning his time at UEFA.The statement came after UEFA confirmed that a “departure payment” was made to a female employee who was allegedly in a relationship with Infantino when he was the European governing body’s general secretary.Britain’s Daily Telegraph reported that the woman received a six-figure sum, while UEFA also covered the fees for an MBA course. UEFA said the payment was “in line” with regulations at the time.A FIFA spokesperson told the newspaper that Infantino “strongly denies these allegations, and they are categorically untrue.”FIFA went further in a lengthy statement on Saturday, hitting back at what it described as “unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims” and suggesting that allegations were being used to weaken Infantino’s authority and force him from office without following the organisation’s democratic processes.“It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its president,” FIFA said.“Those who do not have the support of FIFA’s member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through FIFA’s established democratic processes.“Recent reporting has included unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims concerning FIFA and its president. Speculation and insinuation should not be presented as fact, and repetition does not make an allegation true.”The statement comes at a particularly tense time for Infantino, who has faced growing criticism following his failed plan to commercialise World Cup profits through a proposed subsidiary, the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).Three continents rejected the proposal, while UEFA has emerged as the most vocal critic. Earlier this week, UEFA said its 55 member associations could still boycott FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, despite Infantino apologising over the failed plan.Following a meeting of FIFA’s senior leadership in Morocco on Wednesday, the governing body acknowledged that “mistakes were made” over the proposal but “reaffirmed their full support” for Infantino.Despite UEFA’s opposition, Infantino has retained significant backing elsewhere.South American governing body CONMEBOL said it would not support any attempt to remove Infantino on an accelerated timetable. The Confederation of African Football (CAF) executive committee also expressed its “unanimous support” for the FIFA president.Concacaf, meanwhile, criticised Infantino over the private investor proposal, calling it a “unilateral and egregious act of poor governance” and demanding a full review of his leadership. Mexico, however, backed Infantino and his call to “collectively continue developing football for the benefit of all 211 member associations.”FIFA said it would continue to defend its president and challenge reporting it considers inaccurate.“FIFA welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to distort facts, amplify unsubstantiated allegations or manufacture distractions designed to undermine progress,” it said.“Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading, FIFA will challenge it directly and vigorously.”The governing body added that its focus remained on its 211 member associations and “making football truly global”, insisting it would not be distracted from that mission.
Article Summary: FIFA hit back at 'unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims' UEFA confirmed a 'departure payment' was made to a female employee who was allegedly in a relationship with Infantino when he was the European governing body’s general secretary. FIFA: ‘Repetition does not make an allegation true’

Article Title: Ashmita Chaliha beats Han Qianxi to win maiden BWF World tour title at Korea Masters
Article Text:
Ashmita Chaliha beats China's Han Qian Xi to win Korea Masters title (ANI Image)

Chaliha overcomes slow start

Indian shuttler shows nerves of steel

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Maiden World Tour title after injury layoff

Indian shuttler Ashmita Chaliha scripted a memorable chapter in her career as she won her maiden BWF World Tour title with a stunning comeback victory over China's Han Qianxi in the women's singles final of the Korea Masters Super 300.The 26-year-old from Guwahati overcame a slow start to beat Han 14-21, 21-14, 21-14 in a 53-minute final, underlining her resilience and fighting spirit on the biggest day of her career.Chaliha struggled to find her rhythm in the opening game as Han took control of the proceedings. The Chinese shuttler claimed the first game 21-14, leaving the Indian with little room for error. However, Chaliha responded emphatically in the second game. She raised the intensity of her attacking play, found greater consistency and forced Han onto the defensive.The Indian levelled the match by taking the second game 21-14, setting up a tense decider.The deciding game proved to be a test of Chaliha's temperament. She trailed 9-11 at a crucial stage but refused to let the deficit derail her momentum. Chaliha produced a brilliant late surge, winning the key points and maintaining her aggressive approach to close out the game 21-14 and seal the biggest title of her career.The triumph is particularly significant for Chaliha after a difficult period earlier this year. She was forced to spend three months on the sidelines after suffering a meniscus tear in her right knee. Her return has now culminated in the biggest title of her career, marking an impressive comeback on the international circuit.With the Korea Masters triumph, Chaliha becomes only the fifth Indian woman to win a BWF World Tour Super 300 or higher-level title. She joins an elite list featuring Saina Nehwal, PV Sindhu, Devika Sihag and Tanvi Sharma.
Article Summary: Ashmita Chaliha beats China's Han Qian Xi to win Korea Masters title. 26-year- old from Guwahati overcomes slow start to beat Han 14-21, 21-14,21-14. triumph is particularly significant after a difficult period earlier this year. She spent three months on the sidelines after suffering a meniscus tear in her right knee.

Article Title: Wrestlers head overseas to gear up for Asian Games
Article Text:
Wrestling (Getty Images)

NEW DELHI: With wrestling missing from the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, India’s grapplers have shifted focus to the tougher continental challenge, with the country’s men’s freestyle and Greco-Roman teams leaving for overseas training camps ahead of the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya from Sept 19-Oct 4.The men’s freestyle squad has already left for Armenia, where it will train from Aug 7-Sept 3 under chief foreign coach Emzarios Shako Bentinidis. The team will then travel to Russia for a local competition from Sept 4-6 before returning home. The Greco-Roman team, meanwhile, will travel to Uzbekistan for training from Aug 9-29. Russia’s Gogi Koguashvili, the foreign head coach, will accompany the squad during the camp, a WFI source said.The women wrestlers will continue training at the Indira Gandhi (IG) stadium here for now. They are scheduled to leave for Japan 10 days before the Games to acclimatise. Japan’s Kosei Akaishi is overseeing their preparations.The selected wrestlers for the Asiad have also been accompanied by sparring partners during the overseas camps, ensuring quality training ahead of the continental event.
Article Summary: India's men's freestyle and Greco-Roman teams leave for overseas training camps ahead of the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya from Sept 19-Oct 4. Article Title: Experience has helped me deal with situations better: Khalin Joshi
Article Text:
Khalin Joshi. (File Pic - TOI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Khalin Joshi has spent close to 15 years navigating the highs and lows of pro golf, but his commanding victory at the J&K Open in Kashmir with a tournament total of 24-under 260 offered a reminder that experience, confidence and belief can still bring out the best in him.Joshi dominated the tournament at the Royal Springs Golf Course in Srinagar leading from the opening round, eventually sealing a convincing victory by a nine-shot margin. For the 33-year-old, however, this win was about more than just lifting another trophy. It was a validation of the work that had gone on behind the scenes during a difficult phase of his career. “Having experience is definitely helping. I have been a professional for almost 15 years now and I have experienced a lot of highs and lows and played at bigger tournaments and venues. I deal with situations a lot better now,” said the 2018 Panasonic Open India champion.His success in Kashmir came after his triumph earlier in the PGTI season at the Andhra Open in April, and the Bengaluru golfer believes the confidence in his game is returning at the right time.“I was calm, I believed in my game and I was confident about the practice I had done during the offseason. The reps I put in before starting the second half gave me the mindset to play freely,” he said.Thick rough and wet fairways at Royal Springs following the monsoon made accuracy particularly important. Joshi’s ability to consistently find the fairways gave him an advantage. “Hitting fairways was key. Being a decent driver of the ball gave me an advantage because it gave me more chances to make birdies from the fairway,” he said.Joshi was impressed by the response from the local community. Having finished runner-up at the JK Open four years ago, he noticed a significant change in the interest surrounding the sport this time. “Golf in the region is growing,” he said.
Article Summary: Khalin Joshi wins the J&K Open in Kashmir by nine shots. Joshi won the Panasonic Open India earlier this year. The 33-year-old believes experience is helping him on the golf course. He was impressed by the interest in golf in Kashmir.

Article Title: Once on the verge of quitting, Kamaljeet gets a shot at Asian Games
Article Text:
Kamaljeet

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

PUNE: At the start of 2026, Kamaljeet had set himself a deadline. By the end of March, he would either break into the top three of the Indian team or quit the sport for good. The Rewari, Haryana shooter stayed in the game. Kamaljeet, 22, earned a place in the men’s 10m air pistol team for the ISSF World Cup in Hangzhou, China and also found a place in the Asian Games squad in Japan. He did so by edging past shooters such as world champion Samrat Rana, Varun Tomar and Olympian Saurabh Chaudhary.“I had been shooting since 2019 and had participated in five international tournaments at my own cost (not funded by the national shooting body). But continuing shooting without being in the team would mean spending more money from my own pocket,” Kamaljeet told TOI.Coming from a modest financial background, the shooter said his father, a farmer, had supported his career for seven years. “I could participate in the international tournaments only because he could arrange money by taking loans,” he said. “I was turning 22 this year, so I had to decide whether I should continue shooting or look for a job. I had set a deadline for myself, ” Kamaljeet said.
Article Summary: Kamaljeet, 22, earned a place in the men’s 10m air pistol team for the ISSF World Cup in Hangzhou, China. He also found a spot in the Asian Games squad in Japan. “I had been shooting since 2019 and had participated in five international tournaments at my own cost (not funded by the national shooting body),” he told TOI.

Article Title: Indian hockey mental conditioning coach Paddy Upton turns to AI to break language barrier
Article Text:
Indian team during a training session with Paddy Upton in Eindhoven on Thursday

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: For foreign experts working with Indian athletes, language is often the biggest hurdle. With not every player comfortable communicating in English, overseas coaches and support staff frequently rely on translators within the team. The arrangement, while functional, can make conversations impersonal and, in sensitive situations, cause nuances to be lost in translation.To bridge that gap, Indian men’s hockey mental conditioning coach Paddy Upton has turned to artificial intelligence. Beginning with the upcoming FIH World Cup later this month, the renowned South African mental conditioning expert will introduce an AI-powered digital twin of himself.“It’s new to the sports world,” Upton told TOI in an exclusive interaction.“I would call it a digital twin or a digital version of me. Using artificial intelligence (AI), I have taken everything I’ve written and every conversation I’ve been able to record over 25 years of mental coaching, and trained an AI mental coaching twin of myself,” he explained.Upton spent the last four months developing the WhatsApp-based programme with the help of some of India’s leading AI developers.Explaining the thinking behind the project, Upton, who has worked extensively with Indian athletes, including the men’s cricket team, said the idea stemmed from the limitations he faced while working with players who were not fluent in English.“With some players who don’t have good English skills, I wasn’t able to provide really good mental coaching support because of the language barrier. Previously, I would sit with a translator from within the team. But if it was something deeply personal, I knew it would either get lost in translation or the player would be hesitant because the translator was either a fellow player or a member of the support staff, which meant confidentiality was compromised. ”The players were introduced to the system on Wednesday.Explaining how it works, Upton said, “Now a player can have a conversation with me in Hindi. It’s like speaking on a WhatsApp call. The digital twin is trained to respond in Hindi, while I simultaneously see the English translation from wherever I am. The next day, I can sit with them and have a personal conversation as well.”While the languages are now restricted to Hindi and English, Upton added, “At this stage, it’s only in English and Hindi. This can fairly easily be expanded.”The 57-year-old stressed that the platform is designed to replicate his approach rather than function as a generic chatbot.“It’s an AI version of a personalised mental coach, but it is trained only on my information and speaks exactly as I would.”The timing, he said, was deliberate.“The idea was to have it ready for the World Cup so I could support players in a way that I haven't been able to before.”With a lot of his work with the team happening remotely, Upton believes the technology can significantly narrow the gap between him and the players.“It’s one of those things that's going to take time. The more they interact with it, the more they’ll understand it, and the richer the feedback and support it will be able to provide. It’s a very exciting development and a wonderful use of the technology now available to us,” he said.
Article Summary: Paddy Upton will introduce an AI-powered digital twin of himself at the World Cup. Upton spent the last four months developing the WhatsApp-based programme. The digital twin is trained to respond in Hindi, while Upton simultaneously sees the English translation from wherever he is.

Article Title: Former Indian cricketer Brijesh Patel calls for uniform coaching standards across cricket academies
Article Text:
Former cricketer Brijesh Patel (PTI Photo/Shailendra Bhojak)

BENGALURU: Former India batter Brijesh Patel on Thursday called for greater standardisation across cricket coaching academies, saying the mushrooming of centres has left young cricketers and parents dealing with conflicting advice.Speaking at the launch of the book, Developing Champions in Cricket by Vedam Jaishankar, the seasoned administrator said: “Over the last two decades, we have witnessed an explosion of cricket coaching centres. While this is wonderful for the growth of the game, it has also created a new challenge, a lack of standardisation. Every academy claims to have the best method, while every coach has a different philosophy. Every parent receives different advice and television experts have yet another opinion. The result is often confusing.”Patel stressed that coaching cannot follow a one-size-fits-all approach, with every youngster requiring guidance tailored to their background and abilities. “Youngsters come from every background imaginable. Some come from cities with excellent facilities, while others travel from small towns.Their exposure, culture, skill levels and learning styles are different. A good coach first understands the child before teaching. And equally, a wise parent understands that every child's journey is unique,” he said.Patel also urged coaches and academies to focus on character-building. “Winning matches is important. Producing good human beings is even more important. Today, best practices are no longer optional,” Patel opined.Patel, who started an academy over four decades ago, underlined the need to create a safe and supportive environment for aspiring cricketers. “Parents want their children not just physically safe, but also emotionally secure. They must be protected from unhealthy influences, bullying, and unnecessary pressure. Creating that environment is the responsibility of every academy and every coach,” he added.
Article Summary: Brijesh Patel calls for greater standardisation across cricket coaching academies. Former India batter says mushrooming of centres has left young cricketers and parents dealing with conflicting advice. Patel stressed that coaching cannot follow a one-size-fits-all approach.

Article Title: ECB 'unhappy' as Ireland defy England's policy, host Afghanistan for ODI series
Article Text:
Afghanistan's Rashid Khan. (AP)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) is reportedly unhappy with Cricket Ireland for hosting Afghanistan in a five-match ODI series, even though England continue to play Afghanistan in ICC tournaments.The five-match ODI series between Ireland and Afghanistan began on Wednesday in Bready. According to a report in The Guardian, Ireland's decision to host Afghanistan could affect its future cricket ties with England.Ireland's move has put its relationship with the ECB under strain. England have refused to play bilateral cricket against Afghanistan because of the Taliban regime's restrictions on women's rights.The ECB's stance is based on concerns over what its chair, Richard Thompson, has described as the Taliban's "gender apartheid".However, England continue to face Afghanistan in ICC events, where tournament points and titles are at stake.The ECB's policy is supported by the UK government, but Cricket Ireland has taken a different approach. Ireland has built close ties with the Afghanistan Cricket Board and is hosting five ODIs this month.Under a reciprocal arrangement, Ireland will tour the United Arab Emirates in March next year to play Afghanistan in one Test, three ODIs and three T20Is.England previously played one-off Tests against Ireland at Lord's before the home Ashes series in 2019 and 2023. Next year, however, England have chosen to play Bangladesh in a warm-up Test instead.England's men's team also faced Afghanistan in the Champions Trophy in Lahore last year.While the ECB does not schedule bilateral matches against Afghanistan, it has supported Afghan women cricketers in other ways. This summer, it organised a tour of England for the Afghan Refugee Women's team and invited them to attend the T20 World Cup final at Lord's.Most members of the Afghanistan women's team fled the country after the Taliban returned to power in 2021 and banned women's sport. Many of the players later settled in Australia.Afghanistan remain the only ICC Full Member without a women's cricket programme, but the ICC has not suspended them.Australia, South Africa and New Zealand have also refused to play bilateral cricket against Afghanistan. Ireland, however, has joined the West Indies, Zimbabwe and the four Asian ICC Full Members in continuing bilateral cricket with Afghanistan.The ECB's relationship with Cricket Ireland has already been under pressure. England declined an invitation to take part in the proposed Euro Nations Cup next year, which would also feature Scotland, the Netherlands and Italy, citing a packed international schedule.England's men's team played a three-match T20I series in Ireland last September, but the ECB sent a second-string squad. No further men's matches between the two teams are currently scheduled.England's women's team, however, will host Ireland in a three-match ODI series next month.
Article Summary: England and Wales Cricket Board unhappy with Cricket Ireland for hosting Afghanistan in a five-match ODI series. England have refused to play bilateral cricket against Afghanistan because of the Taliban regime's restrictions on women's rights. ECB's stance is based on concerns over what its chair, Richard Thompson, has described as the Taliban's "gender apartheid" England continue to face Afghanistan in ICC events where tournament points and titles are at stake.

Article Title: After Pakistan boxer, Uganda athletes go ‘missing’ in Glasgow after CWG campaign; police intitate probe

Pakistani boxer Qudratullah

NEW DELHI: Scottish police are investigating reports that several athletes from Pakistan and Uganda did not return home after the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow ended last Sunday.“Police Scotland has ⁠received reports of several athletes who are unaccounted for,” a spokesperson said late on Tuesday, as quoted by Al Jazeera.“Enquiries are ongoing to assess the circumstances, and early engagement is taking ‌place with the Home Office.”Uganda’s NBS Sport reported that four of its six boxers were missing before the team was due to fly home on Tuesday. One of the athletes reportedly told the broadcaster that they planned to seek asylum. Pakistan Today also reported that one Pakistani boxer did not turn up for the return flight.Pakistani boxer Qudratullah has reportedly gone missing in Glasgow just hours before the country’s team was scheduled to leave for home. According to Geo News, Pakistan Boxing Federation sources said Qudratullah was last seen in his hotel room at around 2am.Officials later checked his room but could not find him. The Pakistani team was expected to gather in the hotel lobby at 9am before heading to the airport.His passport and return ticket are reportedly still with the team manager.Cases of athletes going missing after the Commonwealth Games have been reported in previous editions. After the 2018 Gold Coast Games, authorities were still searching for 50 athletes and officials a month later, while another 190 had sought asylum.Pakistan’s 21-member contingent ended the 2026 Commonwealth Games with just one medal. Boxer Fatima Zahra won bronze in the women’s 60kg category, becoming the first Pakistani female boxer to win a Commonwealth Games medal.The result was Pakistan’s lowest medal tally since 1998. Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem also missed out on a medal despite being one of the country’s biggest hopes.

Article Title: WI vs PAK 2nd Test: Babar Azam's wait for Test century continues; Pakistan on brink of victory vs West Indies
Article Text:
Pakistan captain Babar Azam once again missed out on a Test century.

Shafique's 160 helps Pakistan take first-innings lead

Babar Azam

's wait for Test hundred continues

Warrican leads West Indies bowling attack

Pakistan strikes back with the ball

NEW DELHI: Pakistan moved closer to a rare away Test win after reducing West Indies to 103/6 at stumps on Day 3 of the second and final Test. Despite West Indies holding a lead of 60 runs, the hosts have only four wickets left, giving Pakistan the upper hand heading into the fourth day.West Indies ended the day on 103/6, leading by 60 runs with only four wickets remaining.Pakistan will look to dismiss the remaining batters quickly on Day 4 and chase a modest target to secure their first away Test victory since 2023. West Indies, meanwhile, are aiming to complete a 2-0 series sweep after winning the opening Test by 90 runs.Pakistan began the day still behind West Indies' first-innings total of 344, but Abdullah Shafique produced a superb unbeaten 160 to guide his team to 387.His innings helped Pakistan secure a 43-run first-innings lead before the visitors were bowled out.Left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican starred for West Indies with six wickets for 112 runs. He cleaned up the Pakistan lower order after already removing key batters earlier in the innings.Pakistan captain Babar Azam once again missed out on a Test century.He was run out for 88 after a brilliant direct hit from Brandon King ended his 183-run partnership with Shafique.Pakistan were still trailing by 63 runs when the wicket fell.Babar attempted a quick single after pushing the ball into the off side, but Shafique changed his mind and sent him back. King collected the ball and hit the stumps with a flat throw, leaving Babar short of his ground despite a desperate dive.It was Babar's highest Test score in 35 innings, but he is still waiting for his first Test century since scoring one against New Zealand in Karachi in December 2022.Brandon King's brilliant fielding effort came at a cost.The West Indies batter injured his lower back after landing awkwardly while throwing down the stumps. He had to be taken off the field, and it remains unclear whether he will be able to bat on Day 4.Warrican was the pick of the bowlers for West Indies.He dismissed debutant Awais Zafar for 1 before Shamar Joseph trapped Salman Ali Agha lbw. Warrican then bowled Mohammad Rizwan for 18 with the second new ball and later finished the innings by taking three wickets in four deliveries to complete a six-wicket haul.West Indies made a solid start to their second innings as Tagenarine Chanderpaul and Kavem Hodge added 40 runs for the opening wicket.However, Pakistan's spinners quickly took control.Sajid Khan removed Chanderpaul and Amir Jangoo before West Indies recovered through a partnership between Shai Hope and captain Roston Chase.The visitors then lost three wickets in the final five overs of the day. Sajid trapped Hope lbw for 15 and dismissed Jayden Seales for a two-ball duck. On the last ball of the day, Chase lost his concentration and chipped a simple return catch to Ali Usman after scoring 17.Sajid finished the day with figures of 4/32, while Usman picked up 2/29.

Article Title: Pakistan cricketers face two-year PCB ban after playing in ‘unsanctioned’ Zambia T20 league
Article Text:
(Representative Image)

Two-year ban looms for players

Players reportedly left unpaid

More than a dozen former Pakistan cricketers could be hit with two-year sanctions after participating in an “unsanctioned” T20 league in Zambia, with the tournament abruptly halted following intervention from the country’s cricket board.The Asian Legends League in Lusaka attracted several former international players, but the Zambia Cricket Union (ZCU) last week clarified that the competition was “not sanctioned, approved or endorsed” by the country’s official governing body.The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) subsequently said it had taken “serious notice” of the participation of its former players and warned that those who took part without the necessary approvals could face disciplinary action.According to ESPNcricinfo, Mohammad Hafeez , Sohail Tanvir and Umar Akmal were among the players who travelled to Lusaka but ultimately did not play after learning that the required approvals had not come through. Several other former Pakistan cricketers, however, are understood to have participated in matches.The PCB said players found to have participated without the requisite approvals would face two major penalties.“In light of the above, the following disciplinary measures will be taken on individuals found to have participated in the said unsanctioned event without obtaining the requisite approvals from the PCB,” the board said.It listed a two-year ban from the issuance of any PCB No Objection Certificate (NOC) for participation in approved overseas cricket leagues or events, as well as ineligibility for any cricketing, coaching, consultancy, mentoring and/or other assignments with the PCB and the PSL for two years.The PCB added: “The PCB remains fully committed to upholding the ICC regulations and safeguarding the integrity and governance of the game.”Among the former Pakistan players linked with the tournament are Imran Nazir, Yasir Shah, Mohammad Irfan, Rahat Ali, Hasan Raza, Yasir Butt and Rana Naeem Anwar. ESPNcricinfo said it had verified that some, though not all, of the players listed in the Pakistan Panthers squad actually participated in matches.The controversy has deepened with reports that some players and support staff faced difficulties over accommodation, travel arrangements and payments after the tournament ran into trouble.A player, speaking anonymously to Telecom Asia Network, reportedly said the group had been misled by agents who claimed the competition had ZCU approval. The player said participants returned without receiving the financial rewards they had expected and described the episode as a major setback.“The situation is a blow for all the players since they had gone there in order to earn some good money which they haven't obtained, but what they have received instead is a severe punishment from the Pakistan Cricket Board,” the player was quoted as saying.The tournament featured six teams — Pakistan Panthers, Indian Royals, Sri Lankan Lions, Bangladesh Tigers, Afghanistan Pathans and Asian Stars — with players from several nationalities. ESPNcricinfo reported that Pakistan was the only board to have issued a statement specifically terming its players’ participation a violation and threatening sanctions.Kamran Akmal has also reportedly urged the PCB to reconsider the punishment, pointing to the participation of players from other countries.The controversy comes as the ICC has begun taking a closer look at the rapidly expanding global franchise-league landscape.At its July annual meetings, the ICC Board approved the creation of a Franchise Leagues Committee, chaired by former Bangladesh captain Tamim Iqbal, to address issues surrounding the growth and coordination of franchise cricket.For the Pakistan players involved in Zambia, however, the immediate concern is the potential two-year loss of access to PCB NOCs and assignments — a punishment that could have significant consequences for former cricketers who continue to rely on playing and cricket-related opportunities for their income.
Article Summary: More than a dozen former Pakistan cricketers could be hit with two-year sanctions after participating in an “unsanctioned” T20 league in Zambia. The Asian Legends League in Lusaka attracted several former international players. The Zambia Cricket Union (ZCU) clarified that the competition was “not sanctioned, approved or endorsed” by the country’s official governing body.

Article Title: Tony Dodemaide says there’s life beyond super pace trio for Aussies
Article Text:
Tony Dodemaide

CHENNAI: Australia have decided against playing a practice game ahead of next year’s highly anticipated Border-Gavaskar Trophy in India. Tony Dodemaide , who is managing Australia’s development squad that is currently training in Chennai, and is also part of the national selection group alongside George Bailey and Andrew McDonald, explained that the tight international schedule leaves little room for a conventional warm-up fixture.Australia’s fourth Test against New Zealand is scheduled to finish on Jan 8, while the first Test of Border-Gavaskar Trophy is slated to begin on Jan 21.“It gets over about 10 days before the first (Test) here...So we’re playing Test cricket, as soon as the game finishes, we get on a plane and come here and have practice, and then straight into the first Test,” Dodemaide told TOI on the sidelines of an event.However, he added that players who are not part of the playing XI for the final Test against New Zealand will arrive in India early to get accustomed to the conditions. “We need to win the Test match against New Zealand. But the players in the touring squad who aren’t playing in that Test will come early to get more acclimatised,” he said.The five match Test series will begin in Nagpur before moving to Chennai, Guwahati, Ranchi and Ahmedabad.The Aussie pace department may still be relying on the experience of Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins, but Dodemaide said the next generation of pacemen is not too far behind.“Scott Boland, Michael Nesser and Brendan Doggett have been really good for us, while we have some very exciting talent coming through. Jhye Richardson, Lance Morris and Xavier Bartlett have also played some one-day cricket for us. ”Among the younger crop, Dodemaide pointed to Sheffield Shield performers Nathan McAndrew, Lance Morris and Fergus O’Neill, “The challenge for our bowlers back home this summer is to set themselves apart to be the next players to come through,” he said.Dodemaide also highlighted the importance of Australia’s current development camp in India, particularly for their young spinners. The squad has been brought to India specifically to experience conditions that are difficult to replicate back home.“In Australia, we can’t replicate the very dry, red soil and spin conditions. We don’t have the same soil types and find it very difficult to get pitches that are dry at home. But it’s not just the playing conditions. It’s the Indian experience, the heat, the crowds, the crowded places. If these players come back to play for Australia, they’ll have all of that to deal with. This gives them familiarity and allows us to see how they respond to that challenge,” he added.Players like Joel Davies, Jason Sangha, Lloyd Pope and Hugh Weibgen are part of the squad. Dodemaide said the presence of several young players reflects Australia’s belief in their potential. “The younger the players are, the more uncertain it is. But through the Under-19s, they show talent, just as Joel has gone on to play for Australia,” he said.Dodemaide also backed Australian players to continue using the IPL as an important development platform, despite the difficulty of balancing franchise cricket with international commitments. “The IPL is the best T20 competition in the world,” he said. “We love our players going to IPL because that is where they come up against the best players in the world...But it is very hard now, as we all know, to juggle franchise cricket and cricket for Australia,” he added.
Article Summary: Australia have decided against playing a practice game ahead of next year's Border-Gavaskar Trophy in India. Tony Dodemaide is managing Australia’s development squad that is currently training in Chennai. Article Title: As match referee, I would have banned Ganguly for making Steve Waugh wait at the toss: Javagal Srinath
Article Text:
Javagal Srinath

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

CHENNAI: If Javagal Srinath had been the match referee when Sourav Ganguly famously kept Steve Waugh waiting for the toss at Eden Gardens in 2001 Border-Gavaskar Trophy, the former India captain might well have faced a suspension.“I would have banned Sourav for a few games!” Srinath said at EEMAGINE event by recalling the incident, which has been regarded as an act of gamesmanship that disturbed Waugh and the Australian team during the course of the famous series that India won 2-1. Ganguly later said that he couldn’t find his blazer which led to the delay, but that’s highly debatable.Srinath, however, praised Ganguly’s leadership, particularly his ability to nurture youngsters such as Yuvraj Singh, Harbhajan Singh and Virender Sehwag. He felt Indian cricket underwent a major transformation after the match-fixing scandal of the late 1990s, with players developing a collective resolve to restore the game’s image.“There was a bit of a resoluteness in each and every player to really put that image back and then prove the world that cricket is superior, cricket is clean,” Srinath said. He added that leadership came from the top four or five players being on the same page, which helped India not only start winning consistently at home but also turn the corner overseas.Srinath recalled that between 1991 and 1997-98, India struggled to win abroad, but things began changing from 1999 onwards.Looking back at the 2003 World Cup final against Australia, Srinath revealed that he had wanted India to bat first after a discussion within the team. “I was one of the guys who said we should always bat first and then put them under pressure,” he said. But Ganguly had a different view. And once the decision was made, Srinath said the team had to move on, but Australia were simply too strong.He recalled recommending Zaheer to selector Chandu Borde after watching the left-arm pacer take six wickets against Air India while representing the MRF Pace Foundation. When Borde jokingly asked what would happen to Srinath if Zaheer was picked, his response was simple: “If he’s good, he replaces me.”Srinath also revealed that Rahul Dravid was “not the best roommate,” joking about the former India batter’s habit of leaving things scattered, while describing Venkatesh Prasad as extremely “spick and span”.On Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Srinath cautioned against comparisons with Sachin Tendulkar and Virat Kohli, stressing that different eras bring different challenges.“When you judge a player it's just not the white ball, it is the red ball cricket as well. Sooryavanshi is a wonderful talent, I think he’s still too young. I hope he develops the maturity like Sachin and has that strong head on his shoulders like Virat.”Srinath also called for a better balance between bat and ball, pointing to shorter boundaries, bigger bats and less pronounced seams. “Something needs to be done to bring some balance into this game,” he said.
Article Summary: Javagal Srinath says he would have banned Sourav Ganguly for keeping Steve Waugh waiting for the toss in 2001 Border-Gavaskar Trophy. The former India captain praised Ganguly’s leadership, particularly his ability to nurture youngsters such as Yuvraj Singh, Harbhajan Singh and Virender Sehwag. He felt Indian cricket underwent a major transformation after the match-fixing scandal.

Article Title: Australia pacer takes 8/25 as Bangladesh bowled out for 54, lose match by an innings

Bangladesh were bowled out for just 54 in their second innings to lose their three-day tour match against a Cricket Australia XI by an innings and 38 runs, giving Australia’s bowling attack plenty to take note of ahead of next week’s first Test in Darwin.Campbell Thompson was the main contributor to Bangladesh’s collapse, taking eight wickets for 25 runs in the second innings at Marrara Oval. The 22-year-old left-arm fast bowler had taken two wickets late on Friday before returning on Saturday morning to claim six more as Bangladesh lost eight wickets for 35 runs.Marrara Oval, where the tour match was played, is different from Marrara Stadium, which will host the first Test from Thursday.Thompson made his South Australia debut last summer and has played only one Sheffield Shield match and two One-Day Cup games. He had, however, faced international opposition previously when he represented the Prime Minister’s XI against the England Lions in November last year.Bangladesh began the third morning at 15 for two in their second innings but lasted only 17 more overs. Opener Tanzid Hasan was the only batter to reach double figures, scoring 22.Thompson took the first five wickets to fall after beginning Bangladesh’s collapse the previous evening. Off-spinner Corey Rocchiccioli then briefly took over, adding to the six wickets he had claimed in Bangladesh’s first innings.Thompson soon returned to finish the job. He dismissed Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto lbw for a duck before taking the final two wickets with consecutive deliveries.The defeat leaves Bangladesh with four days to prepare for their first Test in Australia in 23 years, where they are set to face Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins and Josh Hazlewood.Bangladesh had scored 263 in their first innings, with Mehidy Hasan Miraz making a century at No. 7 after the top order struggled on the opening day. The CA XI replied with 355, while Bangladesh seamer Hasan Mahmud took four wickets for 42 runs.
Article Summary: Bangladesh bowled out for just 54 in their second innings against a Cricket Australia XI. Campbell Thompson took eight wickets for 25 runs in the second innings. The 22-year-old left-arm fast bowler had taken two wickets late on Friday before returning on Saturday morning to claim six more.

Article Title: Devdutt Padikkal hits century as Pant and Jurel fail, how India's batters fared on day 2 vs SLC XI

Ravindra Jadeja, Devdutt Padikkal

Devdutt Padikkal strengthened his case for a place in India’s playing XI for the first Test against Sri Lanka with an unbeaten 142 on the second day of the warm-up match against Sri Lanka Cricket XI in Colombo.While Padikkal made the most of improved batting conditions, Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel missed their chances to spend time at the crease. Article Title: Why Devdutt Padikkal's fluent ton allows India to breathe easy
Article Text:
Devdutt Padikkal

TimesofIndia.com in Colombo:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Big strides, assured footwork, smart use of the crease, fluent shots and solid defence. These were the highlights of Devdutt Padikkal's unbeaten 142 off 164 balls at the Nondescript Cricket Club in Colombo on Saturday. The classy left-hander was not a starter when the squad was picked for the series. Still, the moment team management received the update on Sai Sudharsan's niggle, all efforts focused on keeping Padikkal ready for the opportunity. When the chance came, he delivered. And how.It wasn't a raging turner, nor were the opposition spinners posing tough questions, but runs always do the confidence a world of good, especially when they coincide with the update on Sudharsan. Since coming into bat in the first over of the second day's play, Padikkal exuded confidence and scored his runs at a brisk pace even when KL Rahul was happy to buy time at the other end.He controlled the ball and showed equal confidence against both spin and pace, remaining unfazed by the off-spin challenge when Ramesh Mendis and Keshara Nuwantha bowled in tandem. He met most balls under his eyes, and the side-on view of his big strides and the balance with which he operated made it a treat.The 26-year-old hasn't featured in a multi-day fixture for India since November 2024 but has been making the right noise with the India A side and Karnataka in the domestic circuit.Keeping the calendar in mind, he specifically worked on his game against spin and spent a lot of time perfecting the craft. Even when the management persisted with Sudharsan as the No.3 bat, Padikkal was busy upgrading. When he played the two multi-day fixtures at Galle last month, the left-hander hit two half-centuries and served another reminder of his readiness.It was more of the same at the NCC; in front of a handful of spectators, the timing was ideal. Before the fixture got underway, there was optimism around Sudharsan joining the camp, if not in Colombo, then in Galle. Little did Padikkal know that as he closed in on a brilliant century, Sudharsan's hopes of boarding the flight evaporated.Come August 15, India won't need to sweat much over the No. 3 position with Padikkal ready and raring to go. A lot of hard work went on behind the scenes, which was reflected in the ease with which he operated.Back in 2024, chief selector Ajit Agarkar's addition of Padikkal to India's Test squad for the home series against England was a surprise pick. The Indian camp was hit by injury concerns, and KL Rahul's unavailability opened the door for Padikkal, who then made his debut in Dharamsala. One knock in the Ranji Trophy was all it took for the chairman to fast-track the left-hander into the set-up.Padikkal would have certainly thanked his stars that Agarkar's rare appearance for domestic games included the Tamil Nadu vs Karnataka game in Chennai.The left-hander, at No.3, hit a 218-ball 151 which included 12 boundaries and six sixes. The opposition had a decent bowling attack featuring the likes of Sandeep Warrier, Sai Kishore and Ajith Ram. It was a classic case of one-and-done, and in the next two years, Padikkal has continued to make opportunities count.A big one has now come his way in Sri Lanka, and the two Tests -- in Galle and Colombo -- present him with a golden chance to cement a spot in India's batting order.
Article Summary: Devdutt Padikkal scored unbeaten 142 off 164 balls at the Nondescript Cricket Club in Colombo. The left-hander, at No.3, hit a 218-ball 151 which included 12 boundaries and six sixes. The 26-year-old hasn't featured in a multi-day fixture for India since November 2024.

Article Title: India's Ruturaj Gaikwad dethroned! England batter sets new List A batting average record

Libby scripts List A record

Worcestershire captain Jake Libby has overtaken India’s Ruturaj Gaikwad to record the highest List A batting average ever. His unbeaten 109 against Sussex, his third straight century with the same score, lifted his average to 61.4. Libby now has 2,456 List A runs, including six centuries and 18 fifties, after 56 matches in the format.Jake Libby has made List A cricket history after his third consecutive century in the ongoing One-Day Cup helped him move past India batter Ruturaj Gaikwad for the highest batting average ever recorded in the format.The Worcestershire captain played a match-winning knock against Sussex on Friday, August 7, staying unbeaten on 109 off 96 balls as his team chased down a challenging target of 334. What makes his recent form even more remarkable is that Libby has scored exactly 109 in each of his last three innings in the competition.His impressive streak started with an unbeaten 109 against Middlesex, helping Worcestershire chase down 294. He followed it up with another 109 against Essex, although his team could not complete the chase after being set a target of 377. Against Sussex, however, Libby once again delivered when his team needed him most.Sussex posted 333-9 in their 50 overs after several batters made useful contributions. Fynn Hudson-Prentice top-scored with 68 from 35 balls, while Jack Leaning added a patient 50. Four other Sussex batters also crossed the 30-run mark, while Freddie Price hit an unbeaten 22 off 13 balls to give the innings a strong finish.Worcestershire made a positive start to the chase, with Isaac Mohammed and Brett D'Oliveira putting together 60 runs for the opening wicket. However, both were dismissed within four overs of each other, bringing Libby to the crease with 251 runs still needed from 210 balls.Libby then took control of the chase and received important support from Kashif Ali, who scored 73 off 52 balls, and Ben Allison, who smashed 20 from just nine deliveries. Together, they guided Worcestershire to victory in the penultimate over.The unbeaten 109 lifted Libby’s List A average to 61.4 from 56 matches, taking him past Gaikwad’s 58.61. He now has 2,456 runs, six centuries and 18 fifties, with a highest score of 126*.Sam Hain is third with an average of 58.18, followed by Michael Bevan, Virat Kohli, Cheteshwar Pujara and Shubman Gill.
Article Summary: Jake Libby has overtaken India’s Ruturaj Gaikwad to record the highest List A batting average ever. His unbeaten 109 against Sussex, his third straight century with the same score, lifted his average to 61.4. Libby now has 2,456 List A runs, including six centuries and 18 fifties, after 56 matches in the format.

Article Title: 'It was a complete lie': Babar Azam refused Irfan Pathan interview? Here's what happened

Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan has spoken about how fake news and online trolling can spread quickly, recalling an incident involving Pakistan cricketer Babar Azam during the 2023 ODI World Cup.Pathan said a false story claimed Babar had refused to give him an interview because of his alleged comments about Pakistan. According to Pathan, the report was created using a manipulated photograph.“The trolling and fake attribution happen every day," Pathan said on JioHotstar.He explained that a Pakistani media outlet had published a story suggesting he had approached Babar for an interview, only to be turned down.“The media in our neighbouring country once ran a story claiming that I had gone to interview Babar Azam, and that he refused because, according to him, ‘He trolls our country, so I won’t give him an interview.’ It was a complete lie. Someone had photoshopped my face onto a picture," he said.Pathan clarified that the person in the original photograph was actually a young Bangladeshi reporter who had approached Babar but was denied an interview.“The person in the original image was a young Bangladeshi reporter who had gone to the ground for the first time and was refused an interview. They literally put my face on his body and spread the story. It got over a million views, and people believed it was me. This happens every day, but I don’t respond. Every day, some lie is told in our name or about some player. If you keep responding to everyone, you won’t be able to live your life," he added.Pathan was part of India’s 2007 T20 World Cup-winning team and was named Player of the Match in the final against Pakistan. He took 301 international wickets and scored 2,821 runs. In the IPL, he played 103 matches, taking 80 wickets and scoring 1,139 runs.
Article Summary: Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan has spoken about how fake news and online trolling can spread quickly. He recalled an incident involving Pakistan cricketer Babar Azam. Article Title: From hospital bed to CWG gold: How Jaismine Lamboria fought the odds in Glasgow
Article Text:
India's Jaismine Lamboria celebrates after winning the women's 57kg boxing final. (AP Photo)
